title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378K (Effect of incorporation of Producer Company)

content.overview: Every shareholder of the inter-State co-operative society immediately before the date of registration of the Producer Company (the date of transformation) shall be deemed to be registered on and from that date as a shareholder of the Producer Company to the extent of the face value of the shares held by such shareholder.
content.glance: On the date of transformation, existing shareholders of the inter-State co-operative society become shareholders of the Producer Company to the face value of their shares.
content.study: Section 378K effects continuity of membership on conversion under section 378J. The date of registration is the date of transformation. Each pre-existing shareholder is deemed a shareholder of the Producer Company to the face value of the shares held. Asset and liability vesting is governed by section 378L, not by this section.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: On the date of transformation, every shareholder of the inter-State co-operative society is deemed a shareholder of the Producer Company to the face value of the shares held.

provisions.title: Effect of incorporation of Producer Company

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378K
examples.body: A member holding shares of face value ₹1,000 in the inter-State co-operative society becomes a shareholder of the Producer Company for ₹1,000 on the date of transformation.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378K?
hypotheticals.analysis: It ensures continuity of shareholding on conversion from an inter-State co-operative society to a Producer Company.

misconceptions.correction: s. 378K deals only with shareholding continuity; vesting is under s. 378L.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378K be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the date of transformation. II. Apply deemed shareholding to face value. III. Conclude.
